generator_metadata.summary: 0-bg SQUARE grid (size 10-30). Top half holds a BLUE (color 1) WALL spanning exactly 3 consecutive rows and the full width. The wall contains 1-3 OPENING pockets: 0-cells with blue somewhere above them inside the wall rows and blue somewhere on both sides in their row (gap shapes: dominoes, squares, L/T/S pieces, ...). Below the wall (>= 1 blank row) sit 3-6 GRAY (color 5) PIECES — 4-connected blobs such as bars, L-shapes, 2x2 blocks, T/plus clusters. Rule (GRAY KEYS THAT FIT A WALL OPENING OR BRANCH TURN RED): every gray piece turns RED (color 2) iff (a) it BRANCHES — some cell has 3+ gray 4-neighbors — or (b) its top rows, taken as tall as some opening, match that opening's shape directly or left-right mirrored. All other cells stay unchanged. Net: keys that fit a lock (or that branch) are marked red; the rest stay gray.

review_brief:
# Review — b6c499e1fa78

Repaired the unapproved base generator for strict controls, exact semantic roles, and lawful 30×30 support, then built a two-setting native family whose default is the byte-exact canonical match-or-branch program. The alternate derives full areas of matching keys and uses that input-dependent set to gate branched keys.

The adversarial pass found and repaired one real constructor defect: a T-shaped decoy opening matched the five-cell plus branch's top slice. The final sampler replaces it with a J-shaped opening, crosses matched-area intermediates against fixed query dimensions, and rejects 13 named partial-intermediate/shortcut rivals at the two-demo minimum. Certificate forgery, duplicate inputs, coercive grid values, private-field leakage, count boundaries, and substantive 30×30 edge contact were also checked.

Focused tests, source-bound authoring preflight, protected causal replay, and single-query export checks pass on the returned bytes. Evidence is finite; owner source review, native qualification/acceptance, and training admission are not claimed.

scope: Accepted generator repair; finite reviewer evidence, no new maintainer execution

sequential_dependency.intermediate: The input-dependent set of full occupied areas of those matching keys; matching tails below the opening-height slice are included.
sequential_dependency.step_a: Identify every gray key whose top rows match a blue-wall opening directly or under left-right reflection.
sequential_dependency.step_b: Recolor every matching key, then recolor a branched key only when its full occupied area belongs to the intermediate set.
sequential_dependency.why_b_depends_on_a: The branch decision cannot be fixed before Step A: at the same query dimensions and profile position, fresh scenes produce matched-area sets {4}, {5}, or {6}, which select different branched pieces. Opening area, bounding-box area, parity, residue, and unconditional branching are separately refuted.
